270268859.privatecomment:
good for 6th grade and older.

Has some violence. Scalping of children and adults. Contains some violent parts consistent with white settler/indian battles. 

In one section on page 88, there is use of "God damn":
"Indian only swear like he learns from white man," the boy said. "My father says when he is a boy he hears white man say God damn. God damn when it rain and God damn if powder don't go off. so my father says God damn too. Then somebody tells him what God damn mean -- that the Great Spirit must burn it in hell fire forever. He is surprise. How could the Great Spirit bother to burn in hell fire forever powder that don't go off? For why would he burn rain when he made rain and sent it on earth? After that my father don't swear. he tells me never swear. It's the white man's lie."

288207367.privatecomment: Follows a young Utah Mormon boy in the mid-1800s who runs away from home and joins a group of Shoshoni Indians. He is adopted by the chief's mother and becomes one of the tribe, learning their customs, and how to become an Indian. There is mild violence in the form of battles and scalpings. Contains death and war and briefly describes a ritualistic practice of mourning, in which those who mourn dismember the tips of their fingers. Not described in detail. He is torn between staying with the tribe and returning home to his family.
